top_temples.name: Baijnath Vaidyanath Temple
top_temples.location_note: 13th-century (1204 AD) Nagara-style temple established by merchant brothers Ahuka and Manyuka; the town's namesake shrine.

top_temples.name: Krishna-Radha Shrine
top_temples.location_note: Subsidiary shrine standing diagonally in front of the main Vaidyanath sanctum, within the same Baijnath Temple Complex rather than a separate standalone temple.

top_temples.name: Markandeya Ji Temple
top_temples.location_note: About 20 km from Bilaspur town; popular with childless couples, with a holy spring and a major Baisakhi fair.

top_temples.name: Vyas Gufa (Vyas Cave)
top_temples.location_note: Ancient cave on the Sutlej river in Bilaspur where sage Vyas is said to have meditated while composing the Mahabharata.

top_temples.name: Chintpurni Devi Temple (Chhinnamastika Shakti Peeth)
top_temples.location_note: One of the 51 Shakti Peethas; the town's defining pilgrimage site.

top_temples.name: Jakhni Mata Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Hilltop temple a short mountain drive from Chintpurni, with panoramic valley views.

top_temples.name: Tsuglagkhang Complex (Namgyal Monastery)
top_temples.deity: Buddhist – residence temple of the Dalai Lama
top_temples.location_note: Largest Tibetan Buddhist temple outside Tibet, in McLeod Ganj; re-established by the Dalai Lama in 1960 after fleeing Tibet in 1959, reflecting Dharamshala's role as seat of the Tibetan government-in-exile.

top_temples.name: Bhagsunath Temple
top_temples.deity: Shiva (as Bhagsunag, with the serpent deity Bhagsunag)
top_temples.location_note: Ancient Hindu shrine near McLeod Ganj, rebuilt in the early 19th century by the 1st Gurkha Rifles; features a sacred spring-fed kund.

top_temples.name: Hateshwari Mata Temple
top_temples.location_note: Ancient temple complex in Rohru district dated to the 6th-9th centuries, linked to the Adi Shankaracharya-era revival of Hinduism.

top_temples.name: Shiv Mandir, Hatkoti
top_temples.location_note: Distinct stone shrine within the same Hatkoti temple complex, housing a large Shiva lingam.

top_temples.name: Jwala Ji Temple
top_temples.deity: Jwala Devi (the flame manifestation of Shakti)
top_temples.location_note: One of the 51 Shakti Peethas, famous for its naturally burning flames rather than a carved idol.

top_temples.name: Baglamukhi Temple
top_temples.location_note: A Siddha Peeth close to Jwala Ji, part of the same regional pilgrimage circuit.

top_temples.name: Brajeshwari Devi Temple (Bajreshwari Mata Temple)
top_temples.location_note: A Shakti Peeth and the most famous temple of the Kangra Valley, often called its gateway shrine.

top_temples.name: Ambika Devi Temple, Kangra Fort
top_temples.location_note: Located within Kangra Fort; considered the oldest Ambika Devi temple in India.

top_temples.name: Raghunath Temple
top_temples.location_note: Installed by Raja Jagat Singh in the 17th century; presiding deity of the Kullu valley and centerpiece of the Kullu Dussehra festival.

top_temples.name: Bijli Mahadev Temple
top_temples.location_note: Hilltop temple overlooking the Kullu and Parvati valleys, known for the legend of its lingam being repeatedly struck by lightning and ritually repaired.

top_temples.name: Bhootnath Temple
top_temples.location_note: Built in 1527 AD by Raja Ajbar Sen; sits at the center of Mandi town, nicknamed 'Chhoti Kashi' for its roughly 80 temples.

top_temples.name: Panchvaktra Temple
top_temples.location_note: At the confluence of the Beas and Suketi rivers in Mandi town; one of the most architecturally significant Shiva shrines in Himachal Pradesh.

top_temples.name: Raghunath (Rama) Temple, Manikaran
top_temples.location_note: Built in the 17th century by Raja Jagat Singh; the principal Hindu shrine in Manikaran's hot-springs pilgrimage complex.

top_temples.name: Gurdwara Sri Manikaran Sahib
top_temples.location_note: Marks Guru Nanak Dev Ji's visit in 1594; devotees take a holy dip in the adjoining sulfur hot springs, sacred to both Hindus and Sikhs.

top_temples.name: Naina Devi Temple
top_temples.deity: Naina Devi (with Kali as presiding deity, plus Saraswati)
top_temples.location_note: One of the 51 Shakti Peethas, built by Raja Bir Chand in the 8th century atop Naina Dhar Hill; huge crowds during Navratri.

top_temples.name: Shiva Shrine, Naina Devi Temple complex
top_temples.location_note: Subsidiary shrine within the same Naina Devi temple complex, alongside shrines to Ganesha and Hanuman.

top_temples.name: Chamunda Devi Temple
top_temples.location_note: Hilltop Shakti Peeth about 10 km west of Palampur on the banks of the Baner river; major Navratri destination.

top_temples.name: Bundlamata Temple
top_temples.location_note: One of the oldest temples in Palampur, roughly 500 years old.

top_temples.name: Raghunath Temple, Rampur Bushahr
top_temples.location_note: Old religious shrine in Rampur town, historic capital of the former princely state of Bushahr.

top_temples.name: Chandika Temple, Rampur
top_temples.location_note: Notable temple within Rampur Bushahr town.

top_temples.name: Bhimakali Temple
top_temples.location_note: A Shakti Peeth and former royal deity temple of the Bushahr rulers, known for its fusion of Hindu and Himalayan pagoda-style architecture.

top_temples.name: Narsingh Shrine, Bhimakali Temple complex
top_temples.location_note: Subsidiary shrine within the same Bhimakali temple complex, alongside shrines to Raghunath and Patal Bhairava.

top_temples.name: Jakhoo Temple
top_temples.location_note: At Shimla's highest point, with a 108-foot Hanuman statue; legend ties it to Hanuman's journey for the Sanjeevni herb.

top_temples.name: Tara Devi Temple
top_temples.location_note: Hilltop temple in the forested outskirts of Shimla.

top_temples.name: Kali Bari Temple
top_temples.location_note: Built in 1845 by Bengali devotees near Mall Road.

top_temples.name: Sankat Mochan Temple
top_temples.location_note: Founded in 1950 by Baba Neeb Karori Ji Maharaj.

top_temples.name: Narvadeshwar Temple
top_temples.location_note: Over 200 years old, built by Maharani Prasanna Devi; walls painted with scenes from the Ramayana and Mahabharata.

top_temples.name: Shoolini Mata Temple
top_temples.location_note: Believed roughly 2,000 years old; Solan town is said to be named after this goddess. Hosts the major Shoolini Fair.

top_temples.name: Jatoli Shiv Temple
top_temples.location_note: Described as the tallest Shiva temple in Asia, near Solan.
